response: **Summary:** The internet originated in the 1960s as a US Department of Defense-funded project, with ARPANET first demonstrated in 1969; the 1983 transition to TCP/IP protocols established the modern foundation, while Tim Berners-Lee's 1989 invention of the World Wide Web and the 1993 release of the Mosaic browser made it accessible to ordinary users. The late 1990s dot-com boom saw massive investment followed by the 2001 crash, though companies like Amazon and Google survived to become hugely valuable. The mid-2000s rise of social media platforms like Facebook, Twitter, and YouTube, combined with the 2007 iPhone launch enabling mobile internet, transformed global communication, while AWS's 2006 cloud computing launch further expanded capabilities. Today, the internet connects over 5 billion people and underpins virtually every aspect of modern life.
